119.51.4.en: May your heart open with love to all people, that you may give them of what God has given you, supporting them, encouraging them and serving them by every means.

119.51.5.en: The ninth section (Teth): Good through discipline (vv. 56-72). The aim:

119.51.6.en: David experienced that the Lord is his portion, and therefore he accepted everything from His hand, even discipline, and felt that it was good for him from the hand of the good God, and he was not disturbed by the plotting of the wicked, or by their growing great against him, but held fast to the word of God.

119.52.0.en: (Thou hast dealt well with thy servant, O LORD, according unto thy word. Teach me good judgment and knowledge: for I have believed thy commandments.

119.52.1.en: Good judgment: sound discernment and right distinction.

119.52.2.en: Discipline: sound principles and good morals.

119.52.3.en: 1- David feels that all God's works with him are for good, whether material or spiritual blessings, or afflictions that teach him sound principles and morals according to God's promise to him, so that he can distinguish truth from falsehood, and has knowledge and principles drawn from the word of God.

119.52.4.en: 2- Because David believed in God's commandments and loved them, he felt that all of them are good for him, so he walked in them with joy, and asked to be a disciple of them and to learn them throughout his life, especially since the Greek origin of the word "well" means "sweetness", that is, David delighted in God's works and in walking in His commandments.

119.53.0.en: (Before I was afflicted I went astray: but now have I kept thy word.

119.53.1.en: 1- David declares with courage that at times he forgot and was occupied away from the word of God, strayed from the way of truth and fell into severe humiliation, then awoke through it, and hastened to the remedy, which is keeping God's commandments. He is a strong person who reviews himself and learns from his sins, and he is positive, hastening to the solution, which is keeping God's commandments.

119.54.0.en: (Thou art good, and doest good; teach me thy statutes. The proud have forged a lie against me: but I will keep thy precepts with my whole heart.

119.54.1.en: 1- The wicked rose up against David and forged false accusations against him, and God permitted this so that David would notice his inner evils and repent of them, as also happened with Job; but the beautiful thing in David and Job is that they turned to God's commandments. David felt God's goodness and kindness, so he turned to the worship of God with longing and kept His commandments with all his heart. This is a good example for the children of God, whom discipline leads to a greater attachment to God and to seeking His commandments, and not to anger or murmuring, for they feel that all things work together for good to them that love God (Rom 8:28), and God's children continue to enjoy the sweetness of His word, which brings them out of affliction while they are in spiritual strength.

119.55.0.en: (Their heart is as fat as grease; but I delight in thy law.

119.55.1.en: 1- The wicked persisted in their evil and in fighting the righteous, and thought that, through the abundance of their material goods, which is expressed by the abundant fat, they were in strength and authority, so they persisted in their evil. And it says that not only their body but their heart has grown fat, that is, their heart has become coarse, not feeling God or the weak, and has become hard and evil, harming others.

119.55.2.en: 2- On the other side we find the righteous, whom David represents, who turned to God's law and loved it, and even delighted in it, so it became their life, and they were not disturbed by the troubling of the wicked, because God gave them peace and even joy in His word.

119.56.0.en: It is good for me that I have been afflicted; that I might learn thy statutes. The law of thy mouth is better unto me than thousands of gold and silver.

119.56.1.en: 1- Since David was assured that God's discipline was a great good for him, in the end he preferred to live by God's law, which is a personal word from the mouth of God to his heart. And God's word is able to enrich him better than all the wealth of the world, which gold and silver represent, and to satisfy his soul better than all the glittering material desires.

119.56.2.en: Teach me, O Lord, to accept affliction since You have permitted it, and to trust that it is for my good. But I ask only that You support me through it and open my eyes to see You in the midst of the affliction, so that I may be comforted by You for all that I endure, and rejoice that I am with You.

119.56.3.en: The tenth section (Yodh): Comfort for those who trust (vv. 73-80). The aim:

119.56.4.en: When the righteous man sees God's goodness through His discipline, he submits to it with trust and surrender, so God's comforts to him increase, and he continues in his repentance, and even becomes an example to the righteous, and walks in the way of perfection.

119.57.0.en: (Thy hands have made me and fashioned me: give me understanding, that I may learn thy commandments.

119.57.1.en: 1- God made me and fashioned me in His image and likeness, but sin disfigures my image, so I always need to learn His commandments that they may restore me to my first image, and in order to learn God's commandments I need to understand; for God created a mind for me, and when I understand it is easy for me to learn God's commandments. This understanding of the depths of the commandment is from the grace of the Holy Spirit.

119.57.2.en: 2- Your hands signify the Son and the Holy Spirit, for the Holy Trinity shared in creation and making, and the making also signifies the creation in the person of Adam, and the fashioning signifies my natural birth from my mother's womb. And the hands signify the power of God, for my creation was a great work surpassing all creatures, and was done by the power of God. The making also signifies my bodily birth, and the fashioning signifies my second birth in the sacrament of Baptism. The making also signifies the creation of man from the dust, and the fashioning signifies the breath of life that God breathed into Adam.

119.58.0.en: (They that fear thee will be glad when they see me; because I have hoped in thy word.

119.58.1.en: 1- Those who fear God, when they see David enduring sufferings and afflictions and waiting in faith for the salvation of the Lord, rejoice at his steadfastness and are themselves established in the faith, and learn steadfastness from David and the surrender of their lives to God, and even see God's works with him and his inner peace, so their joy increases and they learn from him, because David's works while he is in affliction and waiting for the Lord, since they are done in calm and without agitation and in reliance on God, are a light to those around him.

119.58.2.en: 2- Here the fellowship of the believers with David appears, because all are members of one body, all love God and fear Him, so they feel with David who is suffering and waiting for the Lord. And the love of these believers who fear God supports David and encourages him.

119.59.0.en: (I know, O LORD, that thy judgments are right, and that thou in faithfulness hast afflicted me.

119.59.1.en: 1- Since David submitted to affliction and discipline and waited for God's salvation, God opened his eyes and granted him the grace of knowing God's purposes, so he understood that God is just and not harsh in His discipline of him, and that he deserves this humiliation because of his sins and failings. God is just, indeed He is the Truth and cannot err, and he felt that he needed this humiliation in order to be rid of his weaknesses and to hold more firmly to God. Here the extent of David's submission, reliance, surrender and acceptance of God's discipline appears, and therefore his eyes were enlightened and he understood the truth.

119.60.0.en: (Let, I pray thee, thy merciful kindness be for my comfort, according to thy word unto thy servant. Let thy tender mercies come unto me, that I may live: for thy law is my delight.

119.60.1.en: 1- After David submitted to God's justice, His discipline and his humiliation, he asks with the boldness of sons for God's mercy, for it is his only comforter and supporter, indeed it is the secret of his life so that he can pass through sufferings and trials. Therefore he holds fast to God's commandments, and they support him, and even become a delight to him. And so, by the mercy of God, affliction is turned into delight and joy.

119.60.2.en: 2- These mercies that David asks for, he bases on God's promises and words to him, indeed he awaits blessings from God's words and promises, blessings that surpass the mind in eternity.

119.60.3.en: 3- The comforting mercy of God is completed in the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption, and He gives His mercies in His Church by the Holy Spirit.

119.61.0.en: (Let the proud be ashamed; for they dealt perversely with me without a cause: but I will meditate in thy precepts. Let those that fear thee turn unto me, and those that have known thy testimonies. Let my heart be sound in thy statutes; that I be not ashamed.

119.61.1.en: 1- The proud, who are the demons and all the wicked who follow them, rose up and wronged David the righteous with false accusations and false witness. But he was not disturbed by their wrongs, but remained steadfast in his faith, and more than this he was occupied with communing with God and praising Him, using in his communion God's commandments and words. His occupation with God gave him peace, while the wicked were in agitation because of their doing evil, and therefore, when they saw God's joy in him and support of him, they came to shame, perhaps that they might repent, for shame alerts them and pricks them, so they feel the vanity of their evil before the power of God, and return to Him.

119.61.2.en: 2- David asks on behalf of the pious righteous who had turned away from him when he fell into adultery and murder, but when they saw him steadfast in his faith during God's discipline of him, they return to him and are strengthened with him and encourage him, and are encouraged in the way of God; because they saw the wonderful work of God and His support of David who submitted to affliction.

119.61.3.en: 3- He asks a third thing after asking for his enemies and for those who fear God: he asks for himself that he may become perfect, that is, be purified from every sin by continuing in repentance, and hold more firmly to God's statutes, that is, His worship. Thus he is in boldness and strength, far from all shame, and continues his spiritual growth.

119.61.4.en: In proportion as you accept afflictions, God reveals His secrets to you, supports you and works in you with power, so you experience God more than at any other time, and without feeling it you become a light to everyone who sees you.

119.61.5.en: The eleventh section (Kaph): Waiting for salvation (vv. 81-88). The aim:

119.61.6.en: After experiencing God's comfort to His children who trust in Him, they are established in the faith, and therefore it becomes natural for God's children to wait for His salvation, even if they endure many afflictions from the wicked, for God supports them by His testimonies.

119.62.0.en: (My soul fainteth for thy salvation: but I hope in thy word. Mine eyes fail for thy word, saying, "When wilt thou comfort me?"

119.62.2.en: 1- David feels that he is in affliction and suffering greatly, but his hope and steadfast faith are in waiting for God's salvation. This verse shows David's steadfastness in waiting for the Lord, so that his eyes have failed, yet he did not waver from waiting for the Lord, in addition to his trust in the salvation of his God and that He is able to comfort him and give him rest; his longings are intense and his steadfastness great.

119.62.3.en: 2- Perhaps these verses are the feelings of the prophets, the pious and the men of God in the Old Testament as they awaited the expected Messiah. It is also the feeling of God's children in the New Testament who await the Second Coming of Christ, like the Apostle Paul (Phil 1:23). And it is the cry of every person who passes through affliction.

119.63.0.en: (For I am become like a bottle in the smoke; yet do I not forget thy statutes.

119.63.1.en: Bottle: a vessel of skin (a "wineskin") in which water, milk, wine or any liquid is kept.

119.63.2.en: 1- In ancient times they used to hang the skin at the top of the tent with the liquid kept inside it, and they would light wood and fire inside the tent, so it filled with smoke that surrounded the skin and made its color black, and the heat exposed the leather to damage. David likens himself to a skin in the smoke, that is, he is almost spoiled and split and the liquids inside it flow out; yet with all this he is still steadfast, holding fast to God's commandments, waiting for His salvation.

119.63.3.en: 2- It is understood from this that David had been a long time waiting for God's salvation, and his life had been exposed to ruin, so that he almost despaired, but he did not lose his hope, and remained waiting for the salvation of the Lord.

119.64.0.en: (How many are the days of thy servant? when wilt thou execute judgment on them that persecute me?

119.64.1.en: 1- From the intensity of David's distress he asks God, "How many are the days of Your servant?", that is, You know that my life is limited and will end; will You not lift the affliction from me before my life is over? And You know that this distress of mine results from the wars of the demons and the wicked who follow them, so when will You save me from their evils? When will You judge my innocence, and give me rest and salvation, and declare that righteousness is the truth that You seek, and that You reject evil?

119.64.2.en: 2- This is the feeling of all the afflicted in the Old and New Testaments, and it is also the feeling of the souls under the altar in the Book of Revelation, who ask God for vengeance on the enemies, the demons, and the declaration of their righteousness (Rev 6:9)

119.65.0.en: (The proud have digged pits for me, which are not after thy law.

119.65.1.en: Digged pits for me: dug pits for me

119.65.2.en: 1- The proud are the demons and all the wicked who follow them. These rise up against the righteous like David and devise plots for them in order to make them fall into their traps, as the hunter digs pits to catch wild beasts; that is, the demons devise cunning devices to deceive God's children. And this condition is of course against God's law.

119.65.3.en: 2- These plots were laid by the Jews for Christ, as they tried many times to catch Him in a word, and even tried to kill Him several times. All this showed that they are children of the devil, and walk contrary to God's commandments.

119.66.0.en: (All thy commandments are faithful: they persecute me wrongfully; help thou me. They had almost consumed me upon earth; but I forsook not thy precepts.

119.66.2.en: 1- On the other side we find the righteous walking by God's commandments with all faithfulness, unaffected by the evil of the wicked and their false accusations, but asking only for God's help to support them and expose the devices of the devil, and give them victory over the demons.

119.66.3.en: 2- This is what Christ did when He served with all faithfulness, taught the crowds and healed the sick, and when they crucified Him He endured the torments and died, but rose from the dead by the power of His divinity.

119.66.4.en: 3- Verses (85, 86) show the wars of the devil that meet every believer in his spiritual life, but when he walks faithfully in God's commandments, He supports him and helps him, so he triumphs over all evil.

119.67.0.en: (Quicken me after thy lovingkindness; so shall I keep the testimony of thy mouth.

119.67.1.en: 1- David concludes this section with comforting words, as he asks for God's many, unlimited mercies, which are his hope in life, and by which he can live in the midst of trials and afflictions, and even enjoy fellowship with God and rejoice. In addition to this, as he lives with God he has compassion on the wicked, and knows that sin is weakness, so he is not vexed by them, but prays for them.

119.67.2.en: 2- As David experiences God's mercies and care, he not only loves God but also keeps the testimonies of His mouth, which are His commandments and His law. They are also the teachings of Christ mentioned in the Holy Bible. For Christ by His Incarnation is the mouth of God, and more than this, it is all the words of the Holy Bible. And the mouth of God is also the preaching of the Apostles, the priests and all the servants.

119.67.3.en: Do not be disturbed by the wrongs of those around you, but on the contrary seek God's help and hold fast to His commandments and the sacraments of the Church, and you will be strengthened and your heart will be filled with peace, and you will even be able to love the one who wrongs you and pray for him.

119.67.4.en: The twelfth section (Lamed): The word of God is firm, equal and unending (vv. 89-96). The aim:

119.67.5.en: After waiting for God's salvation and enduring the plots of the wicked, the believer enjoys God's heavenly commandments, which are suitable for every generation, and he seeks them, repeats them, understands them, and experiences their breadth.

119.68.0.en: (For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.

119.68.1.en: 1- When David saw the plots of the wicked, their agitation and their rejection of God's word, he looked to heaven, where there is steadfastness. For God is steadfast, and His creatures like heaven are steadfast, and His word is also steadfast, which all heavenly creatures, that is, the angels, hold to. And in proportion as a person holds fast to God's commandments he keeps his peace and steadfastness, and becomes heavenly, and prepared to dwell in the Kingdom. On the contrary, by rejecting God's word the wicked are agitated, and move away from God and hasten to their fixed end, which is eternal torment.

119.68.2.en: 2- Christ is the Word of God, firm in the heavens from eternity and for ever, and He became incarnate in the fullness of time to redeem us, but He prepared for us a heavenly place, and awaits us that we may be lifted up to Him after our life on earth, and remain in Him for ever.

119.68.3.en: 3- God's word and promises, though they seem as far away as heaven is from earth, are firm and cannot change, as Christ declared (Mk 13:31), and must be fulfilled even if after a while. And waiting for God's promises lifts a person's heart to heaven, so he rises above all earthly lusts and lives a heavenly life, pure before God.

119.69.0.en: (Thy faithfulness is unto all generations: thou hast established the earth, and it abideth. They continue this day according to thine ordinances: for all are thy servants.

119.69.1.en: 1- The steadfast God also made His creatures steadfast, not only the heavens but the earth too, with all its conditions of day and night and the four seasons. All creatures, whether the sun, or the air, or the whole earth, are servants of God, that is, subject to Him. And therefore God's word and promises are firm.

119.69.2.en: 2- If God's faithfulness is firm from generation to generation, what is meant is His steadfastness in His care and commandments for the Jewish people in ancient times, then the second generation, or the second age, which is the Church of the New Testament, so His promises and commandments for the Church are firm, and His judgments and word remain firm for ever in eternity.

119.70.0.en: (Unless thy law had been my delights, I should then have perished in mine affliction. I will never forget thy precepts: for with them thou hast quickened me.

119.70.1.en: 1- The prophet David remembers that he had fallen into sin, which caused him humiliation, but when he returned to God and began to recite His word he delighted in it; because He forgave him his sins and even gave him the joy of fellowship with Him. Therefore he promises God not to forget His word for ever, that is, all his life; because God's word is the secret of his life.

119.70.2.en: 2- If Satan wants to make the believer fall into sin, the protection from his wars is in repeating God's commandments and reciting them and delighting in them; by this he lives with God and is fortified in Him, and therefore does not leave God's commandments all his life; even in eternity he will continue to enjoy the word of God, and there the sweetness of God's word will be revealed more and more.

119.71.0.en: (I am thine, save me; for I have sought thy precepts. The wicked have waited for me to destroy me: but I will consider thy testimonies.

119.71.2.en: I will consider: I will understand.

119.71.3.en: 1- Since David delighted in the word of God and was always reciting it, he surrendered his life to God, and said to Him, "I am thine, save me", for I have sought thy precepts, and I will keep seeking them all my life. Therefore the divine grace works in him with power, and keeps him and protects him, however the wicked surround him and try to destroy him, but he held fast to understanding and repeating God's testimonies and commandments.

119.72.0.en: (I have seen an end of all perfection: but thy commandment is exceeding broad.

119.72.1.en: 1- Everything that seems strong or perfect in the world has an end. David saw Goliath the giant, whom no one could stand before, fall by a stone from a sling, and Absalom the commander of the great army die hanging by his hair in a tree. But God's commandments have no end; they are a treasure in which, whenever one reads it, one finds new meanings and thoughts, and not only in the days of David but even today: empires fall and every power in the world collapses, but the word of God is rich, and no one can comprehend all its depths. And all the perfections of the world, that is, the material things that David sees as complete and perfect, are also limited, whereas the word of God is broad and has no limits, because it is connected to His divine, unlimited person.

119.72.2.en: 2- The word of God, His knowledge and His mind is the Son incarnate in the fullness of time, Christ our God, and He is unlimited, whereas all the words of the world and everything great have limits, and Christ our God is above every power in the world and endures for ever.

119.72.3.en: When you read the Holy Bible every day, ask God to reveal His secrets to you, so that you understand new meanings that satisfy your soul, that you may live by them, and so you hear the voice of God as a personal message to you every day. May you memorize the verse that pleased you in order to repeat it always.

119.72.4.en: The thirteenth section (Mem): The sweetness of the word of God (vv. 97-104). The aim:

119.72.5.en: When David realized the steadfastness of the word of God, its loftiness and its breadth, he loved it very much and learned it and held fast to it, so that he hated all evil and falsehood.

119.73.0.en: (O how love I thy law! it is my meditation all the day.

119.73.1.en: 1- David tasted the sweetness of the word of God and loved it very much, so that he repeated it all day, indeed all his life, and his love for it increased, and he kept it, that is, applied it in his life, and experienced new depths in it, and enjoyed it with an enjoyment that cannot be expressed.

119.74.0.en: (Thou through thy commandments hast made me wiser than mine enemies: for they are ever with me.

119.74.1.en: 1- Since David held fast to the word of God, he acquired more understanding and knowledge than his enemies the demons, so he was able to discover their devices and keep away from them, and his holding fast to the word of God increased, and he felt that it is his, that is, his life, indeed he also belongs to it, so he lived by it and its influence on him increased.

119.74.2.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about the Christians, for every believer in the New Testament can understand and know God more than the Jews who crucified Christ and persecuted the Apostles and the Christians, because the believer in the New Testament receives by the Holy Spirit an understanding of the commandment deeper and more perfect than the Jews.

119.75.0.en: (I have more understanding than all my teachers: for thy testimonies are my meditation. I understand more than the ancients, because I keep thy precepts.

119.75.2.en: 1- David learned from teachers and benefited from the elders, but at the same time he was attached to the word of God, kept it and tried to live by it, and he used to repeat it and enjoy meditating on it, so God gave him additional understanding and wisdom, until he understood more than those from whom he learned and than the elders; that is, God gave him in his youth the wisdom of the elders, because he clung to the word of God.

119.75.3.en: 2- David met teachers and elders who knew a great deal of information about the world, and who were not teachers of the Law and the word of God, and he benefited from them, but he learned more, and received great wisdom, from keeping, studying and meditating on the word of God.

119.75.4.en: 3- These two verses apply to Christ, who understood more than the teachers and elders of the Jews; because He is the Word of God and the source of wisdom from eternity, and it is His meditation, and He of course keeps it because He Himself is the Word of God, and the wisdom of Christ appeared when He sat in the Temple among the teachers and all who heard Him were astonished at His wisdom (Lk 2:46, 47).

119.75.5.en: 4- The believers in the New Testament, when they knew Christ the Word of God and kept His word, meditated on it and received more wisdom than all the teachers of the Jews and the elders from whom they learned. For the teachings of Christ are of course the perfect teachings, whereas the teachings of the teachers and elders of the Jews were about the Law, which is a type of Christ and leads to Him. The Apostles were younger than the elders of the Jews in the knowledge of God, but the Holy Spirit granted them wisdom and understanding of the word of God more than the elders of the Jews.

119.76.0.en: (I have refrained my feet from every evil way, that I might keep thy word. I have not departed from thy judgments: for thou hast taught me.

119.76.1.en: 1- David's attachment to the word of God helped him to keep away from evil, and he even loved the word of God to the point that he was concerned to keep it, not only in his mind but to live by it. And however much Satan tried to draw him away from God's commandments, he did not leave them or depart from them; because God taught him through the commandment that it is life, and there is no life without it.

119.76.2.en: 2- In these two verses the importance of spiritual striving appears in David's keeping his feet from walking in evil and not turning aside from the way of God's commandments, and grace granted him this spiritual inclination, and even taught him to live by it.

119.77.0.en: (How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!

119.77.1.en: 1- After David kept away from the ways of evil and was occupied with the word of God, he discovered its sweetness in his mouth, sweeter than every sweetness in the world, which he expressed by honey; that is, he tasted new depths of the sweetness of God's word, so his holding fast to it increased. Thus David shows that the word of God is spiritual food that satisfies the soul, just as bodily food satisfies the body.

119.78.0.en: (Through thy precepts I get understanding: therefore I hate every false way.

119.78.1.en: 1- By continually tasting the sweetness of God's word David acquired the wisdom of "understanding" which made him keep away from everything; that is, deepening in the understanding of the word of God automatically keeps a person away from the ways of evil, and the reverse is true: whoever is lax in keeping the word of God falls easily into evil. For the wisdom a person receives from keeping the word of God surpasses all knowledge, or experience, or intelligence in the world.

119.78.2.en: Do not be content with reading the Holy Bible every day, but may you meditate on the word of God and pray, until God reveals to you the sweetness of His word, so that you are satisfied by it, and the word of God turns into a new life whose sweetness you feel, and its loftiness above the works of the world.

119.78.3.en: The fourteenth section (Nun): Spiritual enlightenment (vv. 105-112). The aim:

119.78.4.en: After enjoying the sweetness of the word of God, David experienced spiritual enlightenment through the word of God, so he held fast to it and pledged to live by it, and it became the gladness of his heart and rescued him from the snares of the wicked.

119.79.0.en: (Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

119.79.1.en: 1- David loved the word of God and tasted its sweetness, so his heart opened to it, and then God by His word lit for him the way of life, which is full of the snares of the demons and the darkness of sin, so he walked in it with wide strides and in peace, discerning good and rejecting evil.

119.79.2.en: 2- Christ the Word of God is the light of the world who lights the way for us, indeed He is the way in which we walk with assurance, holding fast to His commandments and rejoicing in fellowship with Him, so we never go astray.

119.80.0.en: (I have sworn, and I will perform it, that I will keep thy righteous judgments.

119.80.1.en: Perform it: fulfill what I pledged

119.80.2.en: 1- Swearing by the name of God was permitted in the Old Testament so that the believers would be established in God and would not swear by strange gods, and therefore David swore here and pledged to keep God's word in order to live by it, and so walk in the way of righteousness; because there is no way to righteousness and goodness except by keeping the word of God. And it is good for David and for every believer in the New Testament to renew his vows to God every day to keep His word and walk in righteousness through the words of the Holy Bible, even if he repeats one verse throughout the day.

119.81.0.en: (I am afflicted very much: quicken me, O LORD, according unto thy word.

119.81.1.en: 1- David expresses the afflictions he passed through, which drove him to abase himself in humility, asking the help of God, who is able to bring him out of the affliction that almost kills him, by the life He grants him through His word.

119.81.2.en: 2- David's self-abasement expresses his repentance before God for his sins, asking forgiveness and the new life that he receives according to God's promises and His life-giving word.

119.82.0.en: (My soul is continually in my hand: yet do I not forget thy law.

119.82.1.en: 1- David was exposed to death several times at the hands of Saul and Absalom, so he expected death at any moment, and therefore he surrendered his life to God, and said, "My soul is continually in my hand." Despair did not fight him, but on the contrary he lived for God, and clung to His commandments and never forgot them, so he is a wonderful example of positiveness in the midst of afflictions, that is, the afflictions drove him to cling to God and His commandments and to surrender his whole life to Him, so he experienced God's power and reliance on Him.

119.83.0.en: (The wicked have laid a snare for me: yet I erred not from thy precepts.

119.83.1.en: 1- The demons and all the wicked who follow them try to make the righteous fall in plots and snares, but as long as the righteous hold fast to God's commandments, these light their way so that they do not fall into these snares, and guide them in everything, so their holding fast to the commandment increases and they do not stray from it.

119.84.0.en: (Thy testimonies have I taken as an heritage for ever: for they are the rejoicing of my heart. I have inclined mine heart to perform thy statutes alway, even unto the end.

119.84.1.en: Inclined my heart: directed it and made my heart lean

119.84.2.en: 1- If the Jews held fast to the inheritance of the land of Canaan because it is from God, David felt all the more that his true inheritance is the testimonies of God and His commandments, for it is by them that he lives all his life, and he will continue to meditate on them for ever, especially as they give him a joy that remains with him for ever. For this reason he clung to the commandment, and it drew his heart to it, so he inclined to carry it out all his life, and his eyes were on the Kingdom, as the Septuagint translation says, "because of the reward". And he cared for God's statutes, that is, His worship, all his life.

119.84.3.en: When you fall into sin, or are perplexed about some matter, hasten to read the Holy Bible, that it may light the way for you and lead you to repentance and the doing of righteousness, and even define and guide you in all your steps.

119.84.4.en: The fifteenth section (Samekh): God's support (vv. 131-201). The aim:

119.84.5.en: After David experienced spiritual enlightenment through God's commandments, he asked for His support, that he might keep away from the wicked, hold fast to His worship, and live in His fear.

119.85.0.en: (I hate vain thoughts: but thy law do I love.

119.85.1.en: 1- David was troubled by those who waver between good and evil, and hated their evils, and his love for God's commandments increased. And the more he loved God's commandments, the more he was troubled by, and distanced from, evil and all who do it, so as not to share with them in their deeds, and he distanced himself from the agitation in which they live; because he had tasted the stability and peace that he receives through keeping God's commandments.

119.86.0.en: Thou art my hiding place and my shield: I hope in thy word. Depart from me, ye evildoers: for I will keep the commandments of my God.

119.86.1.en: Shield: the shield is the large buckler. And the buckler is a defensive implement consisting of a piece of wood with a loop at the back into which the soldier puts his hand and moves it in front of his face and body to protect himself from the arrows of the enemies

119.86.2.en: 1- Before the wavering wicked around him David feels that their conduct and thoughts hinder him from God, so he flees from them by prayer, where he hides in God and takes refuge in Him, and in his prayer he waits for the word of God, which satisfies him and protects him and covers him. And when the wicked go away from him he has a quiet opportunity to keep God's commandments, meditate on them, and enjoy repeating them.

119.86.3.en: 2- He asks God to take the wicked away from him, that is, his evil thoughts, and he hides and takes refuge by repeating the word of God and delighting in meditating on it

119.87.0.en: (Uphold me according unto thy word, that I may live: and let me not be ashamed of my hope. Hold thou me up, and I shall be safe: and I will have respect unto thy statutes continually.

119.87.1.en: Uphold me: help me and assist me

119.87.2.en: 1- David feels that evil thoughts and the conduct of the wicked almost kill him, but his hope is in God's help according to His promise to him, so that he lives. And by God's support of him he receives salvation, and expresses his love of righteousness in holding fast to holy worship.

119.87.3.en: 2- Here the work of grace supporting striving appears, for David relies on God's grace which drives him in his spiritual striving, and he is also encouraged by his looking to eternity, that is, the new life, where he receives complete salvation.

119.88.0.en: (Thou hast trodden down all them that err from thy statutes: for their deceit is falsehood. Thou puttest away all the wicked of the earth like dross: therefore I love thy testimonies.

119.88.1.en: Dross: the impurities that the craftsman separates from metals

119.88.2.en: 1- In order to live with God, David despised the thoughts and conduct of those who err from God, who went astray because of their holding to evil, vain thoughts, and supposed that they give happiness, although they are all passing material things.

119.88.3.en: He does not despise the erring in themselves, but he despises the error and the evil thought, and regards the conduct of the wicked as dross, that is, worthless impurities, so he keeps away from them and clings to the word of God.

119.88.4.en: And so he keeps away from evil company, lest it corrupt his life (1 Cor 15:33)

119.89.0.en: (My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.

119.89.2.en: 1- When David saw the wicked and the evils surrounding him, he remembered God's judgment, so his body shuddered and he was terrified, and he remembered that God would judge him by His word if he mixed with the wicked, and therefore he fled from every evil and held fast to God's judgments, which give him peace and tranquility.

119.89.3.en: Examine yourself at the end of every day, and remember God's works and care throughout your day in order to thank Him. On the other hand, remember your sins that you committed before the awesome and just God, that you may repent of them, ask His mercies, and promise Him to live a pure life with His help.

119.89.4.en: The sixteenth section (Ayin): Steadfastness and keeping the commandment (vv. 121-128). The aim:

119.89.5.en: After the righteous man has experienced God's support, he asks Him to protect him from the wicked, have mercy on him and make His word known to him, that he may love it and live by it in the upright way.

119.90.0.en: (I have done judgment and justice: leave me not to mine oppressors.

119.90.1.en: 1- David the king walked in the way of God, and established justice in his kingdom and in his judgments, out of his fear of God, as the previous section ended. And he entreats God here to protect him, and not to leave the wicked oppressors to harm him and wrong him, but that God treat him with justice, because God is just and merciful.

119.90.2.en: 2- David here is not boasting when he says "I have done justice", but he implores the just God, who understands him, to protect him from the oppressors, especially since he tried to apply God's commandments and justice, so he asks for God's mercies.

119.91.0.en: (Be surety for thy servant for good: let not the proud oppress me.

119.91.1.en: 1- David asks God in humility to include him in His care, so that He guarantees him good by His mercy, lest the demons and their followers, the wicked oppressors, wrong him. He feels his weakness before the power of the wicked and has no guarantee except God's protection.

119.91.2.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ the Redeemer who offers us salvation and guarantees us good, and delivers us from the hands of the proud demons.

119.92.0.en: (Mine eyes fail for thy salvation, and for the word of thy righteousness.

119.92.2.en: 1- David awaits God's salvation and lifts up constant prayers, and his eyes even pour out many tears, until his eyes fail, but he did not despair, and remained waiting for the word of God that helps him to live in righteousness, for he longs for God and cannot live without His word.

119.92.3.en: 2- David lifted his eyes in the spirit of prophecy, awaiting the salvation that Christ would accomplish in the fullness of time on the Cross, and he sees the righteous, holy Word redeeming mankind, and so He gladdens the hearts of all who awaited Him in the Old Testament, and likewise the believers in Him in the New Testament.

119.93.0.en: (Deal with thy servant according unto thy mercy, and teach me thy statutes. I am thy servant; give me understanding, that I may know thy testimonies.

119.93.1.en: 1- In humility David asks for God's care and tending of him according to God's mercy, and not according to his deserving; for he feels that he deserves nothing because of his many sins. And he longs to receive spiritual understanding, so as to hold fast to the worship of God, which is His statutes, and likewise His testimonies, which are His word.

119.93.2.en: 2- In proportion as a person asks God to give him understanding, God's mercies and wisdom are poured out upon him. For God gives to His children according to their sense of need of Him, their faith in Him, and their love for Him shown in many prayers.

119.94.0.en: (It is time for thee, LORD, to work: for they have made void thy law.

119.94.1.en: 1- David felt that people had turned away from God's law and His Law, as they plunged into many sins. So he was jealous with the zeal of God, and felt that he must work with all speed and power to proclaim the name of God and bring souls back to Him, that is, the necessity of service and of preaching the name of God, to bring His children back to Him.

119.94.2.en: 2- David says this verse in the spirit of prophecy about Christ, that is, Christ says in the fullness of time that it is a time to work for the Lord, that is, to offer Himself on the Cross after He preached and performed many miracles, to draw the distant souls that had forsaken God's law.

119.95.0.en: (Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold. Therefore I esteem all thy precepts concerning all things to be right; and I hate every false way.

119.95.2.en: 1- David loved God's commandments, so he acted by them, and they made his life upright and kept him away from the ways of falsehood and evil. So he hated the evil, crooked ways, and each day he grew in holding fast to God's commandments because they are upright, and they raise up and correct his life whenever he lives by them.

119.95.3.en: 2- When David loved God's commandments this helped him to apply them, especially as he loved them more than gold, from which the most precious idols are made. For the worship of God is above all worships and gods. And also God's commandments are better than all the lusts and material things of the world, even the precious among them, such as gold.

119.95.4.en: Today is an acceptable day and the hour is an hour of salvation, so may you rise to live in God's commandments, to experience them and enjoy them, and then you will be able to teach them to those around you, because they have departed from God and His word and plunged into the lusts of the world, and are in great need to see a living picture of God's children who live by His word.

119.95.5.en: The seventeenth section (Pe): Wonderful effects (vv. 129-136). The aim:

119.95.6.en: Steadfastness in the word of God drove the righteous man to enter into the depths of the commandment, so he discovered its various effects in enlightenment, keeping away from sin, keeping the commandment, and grief over sinners

119.96.0.en: (Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore doth my soul keep them.

119.96.1.en: 1- David feels that God's words are wonderful, because they revolve around one idea despite the different times of their writing, and this idea is Christ the Savior, wonderful in His works, as Isaiah mentioned (Isa 9:6). And whenever we read them and meditate on them we find new depths; because God is unlimited and the depths of His word have no end.

119.96.2.en: 2- God's testimonies are also His works in all creation, which speak of His glory, and meditating on them shows us the greatness of God and His love. Therefore David kept them, not in his thought only but in his soul, that is, with his thought and feelings, so they lived within him and influenced his works and all his life.

119.97.0.en: (The entrance of thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple.

119.97.1.en: 1- David felt that he was a beginner in his knowledge of the word of God. And that he opened his mind to understand the word of God, and was enlightened by it. And he saw in the spirit of prophecy that Christ, who is the Word of God, would come in the fullness of time and give salvation to mankind, and so would reveal new depths of the word of God, and the divine revelations about the word of God increase in eternity. And whenever a person reads the word of God it gives him a blessing and a new understanding according to his need and his longing to know God.

119.97.2.en: 2- Those who are enlightened are the simple, or the plain, or the children, that is, those who feel their ignorance and weakness, so God grants them His knowledge, whereas the proud know nothing, and live in superficiality and a philosophy that avails nothing, for they do not enter into the depths of the word of God or even understand it, but are prisoners of their minds, and not subject to God, that He may give them understanding.

119.98.0.en: (I opened my mouth, and panted: for I longed for thy commandments.

119.98.1.en: Opened: I opened. Panted: I put out my tongue from intense thirst and weariness.

119.98.2.en: 1- In great humility David declares his thirst for the water of life, which is the word of God, saying, I have opened my mouth, and shown my thirst for the word of God and my need for the air I breathe, which is the Spirit of God; that is, the word of God is the water, the air and the life for which David longs. And he declares his inability to obtain it by himself; therefore he opens his mouth for God to give him.

119.98.3.en: 2- This verse is declared by the priest on the day of his ordination, and he repeats it according to the Septuagint translation, "I opened my mouth and drew in the Spirit for myself", and he opens his mouth, and the Father the Patriarch, or the bishop, breathes into his mouth so that he may receive the Holy Spirit, and receive a special grace to practice the sacrament of the priesthood with all its responsibilities. So the priest declares his need of the Holy Spirit and the word of God, for which he longs like David.

119.99.0.en: (Look thou upon me, and be merciful unto me, as thou usest to do unto those that love thy name.

119.99.1.en: 1- David continues to declare his weakness and his need of God, and asks Him to look upon him; because the mere looking of God upon him gives him all blessings. This look is according to God's mercy and not according to David's deserving, and this confirms David's humility.

119.99.2.en: 2- God has mercy on those who love His name, who are those who repent of their sins and walk in righteousness, and David declares his repentance and tries to walk in righteousness; therefore he entreats God to have mercy on him. And when he says "as thou usest to do unto those that love thy name" he does not mean that this is his right, and demand it from God as if he were God's creditor, but he means to express his need, as one who loves God, of His forgiveness and support, that he may live in righteousness and virtue.

119.100.0.en: (Order my steps in thy word: and let not any iniquity have dominion over me.

119.100.1.en: 1- David also asks God to establish him in reading His word, meditating on it, repeating it and turning it into conduct; because by this steadfastness evil does not have dominion over him, and even if a sin fights him, or he falls into it, he hastens to repentance to live by the word of God, that is, the word of God protects him from sin, and the more he is established in it, the higher he rises above evil.

119.101.0.en: (Deliver me from the oppression of man: so will I keep thy precepts.

119.101.1.en: 1- David asks God to redeem him and rescue him from the oppression of man, that is, those who are hostile to him and try to kill him, like Saul and his men, so that he can go to the house of God and draw near to Him, and this helps him to keep His commandments. In this he does not murmur against the affliction, but asks for a wider opportunity to keep God's commandments, and God is able within the affliction to give him peace, and strength to keep His commandments and not be hindered because of the affliction, or fall into various sins, but to be established in God's commandments.

119.101.2.en: 2- David looked in the spirit of prophecy and saw Christ the Savior and Redeemer, who is able to deliver him from the oppression of the wicked behind whom the devil hides, that is, to deliver him from the oppressing demons, and this gives him an opportunity to keep God's commandments.

119.102.0.en: (Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; and teach me thy statutes.

119.102.1.en: 1- David entreats God to make His face shine upon him, that is, to look upon him, and God is the source of light, so David is enlightened, and then he learns His judgments from God.

119.102.2.en: 2- David declares that he is the servant of God, that is, His follower, and this confirms his humility, and his love of God, and that any enlightenment David receives is not from himself but from God. And then he cares for and tends those around him, giving them of what God has given him, that is, he gives this enlightenment and the teaching of the word of God in humility.
